See also: bisturí

Albanian

[edit]
Albanian Wikipedia has an article on:
bisturi
Wikipedia sq

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French bistouri, from archaic Italian pistorese or pistorino (“from Pistoia”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /bis.tuˈɾi/
  • Rhymes: -i

Noun

[edit]

bisturi f (plural bisturi, definite bisturia, definite plural bisturitë)

  1. (surgery) scalpel, lancet, bistoury

Declension

[edit]
Declension of bisturi
singular plural
indefinite definite indefinite definite
nominative bisturi bisturia bisturi bisturitë
accusative bisturinë
dative bisturie bisturisë bisturive bisturive
ablative bisturish

Indonesian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Dutch bistouri, from French bistouri, from archaic Italian pistorese or pistorino (“from Pistoia”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /bisˈturi/ [bisˈt̪u.ri]
  • Rhymes: -uri
  • Syllabification: bis‧tu‧ri

Noun

[edit]

bisturi (plural bisturi-bisturi)

  1. (surgery, colloquial) scalpel; blade; medical knife
    Synonyms: mes, pisau bedah, pisau operasi, skalpel

Italian

[edit]
Italian Wikipedia has an article on:
bisturi
Wikipedia it

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • bistori, bisturì (rare)
  • bistorì, bisturino, bistorino (dated)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French bistouri, in turn from archaic Italian pistorese or pistorino (“from Pistoia”, see Latin Pistōrium); the city of Pistoia was once famous for the manufacturing of blades. Doublet of pistoiese.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbis.tu.ri/
  • Rhymes: -isturi
  • Hyphenation: bì‧stu‧ri

Noun

[edit]

bisturi m (invariable)

  1. (surgery) scalpel, bistoury, lancet

Derived terms

[edit]
  • elettrobisturi

Further reading

[edit]
  • bisturi in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

Anagrams

[edit]
  • buristi, subirti

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French bistouri, from archaic Italian pistorese or pistorino (“from Pistoia”).

Pronunciation

  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /bis.tuˈɾi/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /bis.tuˈɾi/

  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /biʃ.tuˈɾi/

  • Rhymes: -i
  • Hyphenation: bis‧tu‧ri

Noun

[edit]

bisturi m (plural bisturis)

  1. (surgery) scalpel (small straight knife)

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French bistouri,[1] from archaic Italian pistorese or pistorino (“from Pistoia”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /bis.tuˈɾi/
  • Hyphenation: bis‧tu‧ri

Noun

[edit]

bisturi (definite accusative bisturiyi, plural bisturiler)

  1. (surgery) scalpel
    Synonyms: neşter, skalpel
